items.title: Pricing Alignment
items.note: Context: the 8/31 Liferun sales onboarding found GoHighLevel subscription and add on pricing out of step with the website, with the website named as source of truth. Sierra starts taking inbound ad calls the next day and quotes from these numbers, so a rep can quote one price while Stripe charges another. Deliverable: audit and correct every plan and add on in the GHL catalogue against the website, then verify through real test checkouts that Stripe captures the right amount. Dependencies: none external, can start immediately; Sohib's payment walkthrough for Sierra should be recorded after this lands. Done: catalogue matches the website and three test checkouts capture correctly. Board audit 2026-09-01 across all four boards with subitems: the Liferun CRM group holds HANDOFF, BWS Verification, Shippo Test, QA Reroute, Becklar Deactivation and Return Automation, none of which touch pricing or payment configuration; Liferun on Ads is Meta Ads, Google Ads and Reports, on Web + SEO is Website, Reports and GBP, and Liferun has no Video presence. Nothing matching anywhere, so this drafts as a new CRM item.

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. The 31 August Liferun sales onboarding session surfaced a live mismatch between the subscription prices configured in GoHighLevel and the prices published on the Liferun website. Sierra Felicidad joins as the sales rep taking inbound Meta and Google Ads calls and starts quoting from these numbers immediately, so a rep can currently quote one price on a call and the Stripe checkout can charge another.
  • The website is the source of truth. Where GoHighLevel and the website disagree, the website wins and GoHighLevel gets corrected to match. Do not resolve a mismatch the other way round by editing the website to fit a GoHighLevel product.
  • Audit and correct every plan and add on in the GoHighLevel product catalogue against the website: the monthly plan and its device fee, the annual monitoring plan sold with free device and free shipping, and the paid add ons including fall detection. Prices quoted in the session ranged from roughly $40 per month up to $359 and $479 on the annual plans, and those figures did not line up cleanly, which is exactly the gap to close. Take the current website as the reference and correct the catalogue, do not work from the numbers in this note.
  • Verify through Stripe, not just in the catalogue view. Run a real test checkout for one monthly plan, one annual plan, and one plan with an add on attached, and confirm the amount Stripe actually captures matches the website. A corrected product record that still has a stale price object attached in Stripe will keep charging the old amount.
  • Dependencies and constraints. No third party dependency, this can start immediately. Sohib owes Sierra a payment processing walkthrough covering subscriptions and add ons, and that walkthrough should be recorded after this correction lands rather than before, so it does not document the wrong prices. Prorated refunds and the no contract policy stay as they are, this item does not change commercial terms, only the configured amounts.
  • done = every Liferun plan and add on in GoHighLevel matches the published website price, and a test checkout on a monthly plan, an annual plan and an add on captures the correct amount in Stripe, with the three test results posted here.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

Per the prerequisite rule in drafting-rules.md the account creation and the routing change are drafted as one item with explicit sequencing rather than as two, because assigning ownership to a user record that does not exist fails silently. Deliverable: confirm the account, set Sierra as primary owner and routing target for paid inbound, reconfirm source tagging and missed call logging, then live test through Lead Connector on her handset. Dependencies: internally blocked on Sohib issuing the email and GHL credentials. Done: live test calls on both channels ring her, tag correctly and land in her pipeline with her as owner. Board audit 2026-09-01 across all four boards with subitems: no existing Liferun item on CRM, Ads, Web + SEO or Video covers call ownership or lead routing; the CRM group's live items are HANDOFF, BWS Verification, Shippo Test, QA Reroute, Becklar Deactivation and Return Automation. Nothing matching anywhere.

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. Sierra Felicidad is joining Liferun as the sales rep who answers every inbound call generated by Meta Ads and Google Ads, and she is expected to start taking those calls from 1 September. Today those calls are not pointed at anyone in particular in GoHighLevel, so without this change her first day produces unrouted calls and leads with no owner.
  • Step one, confirm the account exists. Sierra's new Liferun email account and her GoHighLevel user need to be created and confirmed working before anything is pointed at her. Do not start step two before step one is done, assigning ownership to a user record that does not exist yet fails silently and the calls simply go nowhere.
  • Step two, make Sierra the owner of paid inbound. Set her as primary owner and routing target for inbound calls attributed to Meta Ads and Google Ads so those calls funnel to her rather than round robin across the account. Existing customer service traffic and returns stay with the customer service rep and must not be rerouted.
  • Step three, confirm tagging still holds. Calls are tagged by source on arrival and missed calls are logged automatically. Confirm both still behave once ownership changes, and that a contact is still tagged as new lead or existing customer correctly, since the follow up automation of up to three touches per week keys off those tags.
  • Step four, test on her device. Sierra takes calls through Lead Connector on her phone. Place a live test call through a Meta Ads number and a Google Ads number, confirm both ring on her handset, confirm a missed call is logged with its source, and confirm the resulting contact lands in her pipeline with her as owner.
  • Dependencies. Blocked internally on the Liferun email account and GoHighLevel credentials being issued to Sierra, which sits with Sohib. No third party dependency beyond that. Related but separate: the subscription pricing in GoHighLevel is being corrected on its own item, and the downstream fulfillment pipeline is being verified on another, neither is in scope here.
  • done = a live test call placed through both a Meta Ads and a Google Ads number rings Sierra on Lead Connector, the resulting contact carries the correct source tag with Sierra as owner, and a deliberately missed test call is logged against the right source.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

items.title: Fulfillment Pipeline Test
items.note: Context: the 8/31 Liferun sales onboarding asked for a verification pass over the automation downstream of a closed deal, covering pipeline stage transitions and notifications through payment, device activation, setup call and shipping, before real orders start flowing from Sierra's calls. Deliverable: drive one dummy contact from closed won to shipped and confirm every stage transition, notification recipient and the post sale data collection. Dependencies: the GHL pricing correction should land first so a test checkout represents a real order. Done: every stage observed and every notification confirmed delivered, pass or fail posted per stage. Board audit 2026-09-01 across all four boards with subitems: Shippo Test (12472536053, Ongoing) owns label generation, label detail, tracking writeback and the shipping SOP, which is the label mechanics rather than the pipeline stages and notifications, and Return Automation (12472536320) and Becklar Deactivation (12472536909) own the return and deactivation paths. Per the merge counter rule in drafting-rules.md these are different kinds of work from a stage and notification audit, so this drafts as a separate item with Shippo Test named explicitly as out of scope rather than folded into it. Nothing on Ads, Web + SEO or Video touches this.

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. With Sierra taking live sales calls from 1 September, Liferun starts closing deals through the GoHighLevel pipeline again, and the automation that runs after a deal closes has not been exercised end to end since it was built. The 31 August onboarding session flagged the whole downstream path as needing a verification pass before real orders start flowing through it.
  • Walk one test deal through every stage. Take a dummy contact from closed won through Stripe payment, device activation, the customer setup call, and shipping, and confirm the opportunity actually moves stage by stage rather than stalling in the stage it was closed in. Record which stage each transition lands in.
  • Confirm every notification fires and reaches a real person. Each stage transition should notify whoever owns the next action, and the customer service rep handles fulfillment and follow up rather than the sales rep. A notification that fires into an unwatched inbox is the same as no notification, so check the recipient as well as the trigger.
  • Confirm the post sale data collection runs. Emergency contact and medical information is gathered after the sale, not during it, and that collection is part of this path. A device that ships without those details on file is not a completed order.
  • Dependencies and scope. Depends on the GoHighLevel pricing correction landing first, since a test checkout against a wrong price object will not represent a real order. Do not duplicate Shippo Test (12472536053), which owns label generation, label detail verification, tracking writeback and the shipping SOP. This item is the pipeline stages and notifications around that work, not the label mechanics themselves. Return and deactivation paths stay on Return Automation and Becklar Deactivation.
  • done = one dummy contact has been driven from closed won to shipped with every pipeline stage transition observed, every stage notification confirmed delivered to the right owner, and the post sale data collection confirmed to have run, with the pass or fail of each stage posted here.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

items.title: Appointment Status Sync
items.note: Section 19b axis 3 match at score 1.00 against this card’s own subject, so merged rather than drafted as a second card. The 4 September go live call reports the sync as accurate while its own action list still carries fix and monitor for Confirmed, No Show and Canceled, so the item is narrowed from a fresh build to a verification pass. Priority dropped from 1 to 2 because the sync mechanism is no longer reported broken.
items.sourceLabel: Meeting with MedStation, 9/3 + Meeting with MedStation, 9/4

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context, where this started. At the go live call on 3 September the appointment status arriving from NextGen was confirmed broken in two separate ways. Statuses came across mostly as the default value, Confirmed did not map onto anything in GoHighLevel at all, and Showed was firing on appointments whose date had not yet happened. Review requests were paused rather than risk asking a patient about a visit they had not attended.
  • What changed by 4 September. At the following morning’s go live call the sync was reported as accurate. Duplicate records are now handled at the DigitalOcean webhook level rather than downstream, and show, no show and last visit date were described as updating in real time, which is what both the reactivation and the review triggers key off.
  • What is still open. That same call still carries fixing and monitoring appointment status synchronisation as an action, specifically that Confirmed, No Show and Canceled all update correctly. The 3 September mapping failure was specific to Confirmed, and nothing since has reported that particular mapping as fixed. Treat the sync as improved but unverified rather than done.
  • Deliverable, verify each status end to end. Book a test appointment and walk it through confirmed, attended, no show and cancelled in NextGen, checking after each change that GoHighLevel shows the matching status inside the sync window and that no status arrives as the default value.
  • Then unpause the review requests, but only once Showed is confirmed to fire on the appointment date and not before it. That was the reason they were paused and it is the only condition for restarting them.
  • Dependencies and constraints. No client dependency, this can start immediately. Do not reintroduce deduplication logic inside GoHighLevel, it is handled at the webhook now and a second layer will fight it.
  • done = each of the four appointment statuses set in NextGen appears correctly in GoHighLevel within the sync window on a single test appointment, none arrive as the default, and review requests are running again.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context, widening this item. This item currently reads as Patient ID alone. On 3 September Sohib flagged in the GHL Dev chat that the gap is broader: a contact arrived that day, Ana Carolina Rocha, NextGen Person ID 3f0e6c04 3cc4 421e b503 d36593484740, with contact source NextGen and every booking tracking field blank. Nothing on the record said which clinic she belongs to.
  • Why it matters. Anything that does not arrive through the booking flow currently lands with no clinic, no service and no history, which makes those patients invisible in reporting and unroutable by any workflow that branches on clinic. A second live case is open on the same day: Sohib asked in the MedStation GoHighLevel chat how the new patient Tania was entered and there is still no answer on the record itself.
  • Deliverable. Make the NextGen to GoHighLevel sync populate all five fields on every contact and appointment it creates, not just those that came through the booking flow: booking clinic, service category, appointment status, first visit date and Patient ID. Trace where each one drops today and fix it in the Digital Ocean sync.
  • Confirm the Weston assumption. Sohib believes Ana Carolina Rocha is Weston because a Weston filter exists. Confirm on this item whether that filter is what actually assigns the clinic, and say where it lives, in Digital Ocean or elsewhere. If a filter is silently assigning clinic without the field being written, that is a reporting problem in its own right and needs saying out loud.
  • Dependencies and constraints. Same Digital Ocean backend as the appointment status mapping work, so the two can be deployed together, but keep the status value defects on their own item. No client dependency, this can start immediately. Do not backfill historical records until the forward sync is confirmed correct.
  • done = a newly synced NextGen contact and its appointment both carry booking clinic, service category, appointment status, first visit date and Patient ID, the Ana Carolina Rocha record has been corrected, and the clinic assignment mechanism is documented on this item.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

items.title: Lead Escalation Workflows
items.note: Merged rather than drafted separately. The 4 September go live call added the missed message trigger condition and the business hours gate, which are refinements of the workflows this card already specifies, so per the single item bias they belong in it. The section 19b matcher returned no match because the short candidate text scores below the similarity bar against this card’s long body, not because the work is distinct.
items.sourceLabel: Meeting with MedStation, 9/3 + Meeting with MedStation, 9/4

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. The 3 September MedStation go live call moved lead escalation off user assignment triggers and onto message status triggers, and Sohib wrote the build out as point three of his recap in the GHL Dev chat the same day. Today a lead who calls and gets no answer, or texts and gets no reply, falls through with nobody told about it. The 4 September call then specified the trigger conditions, which are carried below.
  • Workflow one, missed call textback. Build it to the same pattern already running for Maadi Law: an inbound call that is not answered triggers an automatic message back to the caller. Reuse the Maadi Law build as the reference rather than starting from a blank workflow.
  • Workflow two, missed message textback. Trigger on a lead sending us a message that nobody replies to inside the escalation window, and send an automatic acknowledgement. This is the half that does not exist anywhere yet, so it needs specifying as well as building.
  • The escalation window, settled on 4 September. The internal alert must fire only when no staff reply has been sent within one hour of the patient’s message. As currently built the notification triggers on the contact replying at all, which means the team is alerted even when somebody has already answered. Correct that condition, it is the specific defect named on the call.
  • Business hours, one condition not two workflows. The one hour timer applies during business hours only, 8am to 5pm Eastern, Monday to Friday. Outside those hours the alert waits until the next business morning rather than disturbing anyone. Handle this as a condition inside each workflow, not as a separate after hours workflow, which is how the same point was decided for the other messaging workflows on this board.
  • Delivery channel. WhatsApp is the priority channel over SMS for both workflows, matching how MedStation patients actually reach the clinic. Where the 24 hour WhatsApp window has closed, this needs the approved re opening template tracked separately on this board, so wire that dependency rather than silently falling back to SMS.
  • Internal notification. Both workflows raise an internal alert to Renata so a human picks the lead up. Confirm the alert actually reaches her rather than only appearing in the GoHighLevel activity feed. Sohib owes the Ads and CRM side sample copy for the missed call and missed message text backs.
  • Dependencies and constraints. Depends on the 24 hour window opening template for out of window sends. Does not depend on the appointment status work. Do not reuse the old user assignment trigger, it is being retired by this change.
  • done = a deliberately missed test call and a deliberately unanswered test message each produce an automatic WhatsApp reply to the lead and an internal alert that Renata confirms she received, the alert does not fire when a staff member replies inside the hour, and all test results are posted here.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

items.sourceLabel: WhatsApp: Web and SEO, 9/3 + WhatsApp: Web and SEO, 9/4

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context, and it is now urgent. This item captured four payment sync decisions Sohib settled on 3 September. On 4 September Hashir deployed the webhook security fix and tested the live checkout end to end, and it failed. That moves this from a configuration task to a live revenue defect, so the test result leads and the decisions follow it.
  • The failing test, 4 September. Hashir ran a real purchase through the live checkout on the Monthly plan, using a temporary coupon to bring it to one dollar. The payment went through on Stripe’s side and the customer was redirected to the Thank You page successfully. The order was not created in WordPress and nothing reached GoHighLevel. Liferun is therefore taking money right now and producing no order and no contact.
  • Where to look first. The Stripe webhook call to the site is failing after payment. Open Stripe Dashboard, Developers, Webhooks, the endpoint pointing at liferun.com, and read the most recent event log entry from that test. Confirm whether it was delivered or failed, and record the exact error or response shown. Prime suspect is the signing secret, because this item had that secret rotated after it was posted into the Web and SEO chat, and a rotated secret that was not updated on the receiving end produces exactly this signature: payment succeeds, webhook rejected, no order.
  • Decision one, Fall Detection is not an upsell. GoHighLevel will not sell a plan and Fall Detection together on a single payment link. Sohib rejected a post checkout upsell, because Fall Detection is decided on the call at the point of purchase. Build it as either a 10 dollars per month add on subscription attached alongside the chosen plan, or as duplicate subscription products per payment type, meaning annual, semi annual and monthly each with Fall Detection. Pick whichever GoHighLevel supports cleanly and say which you used.
  • Decision two, the semi annual price is wrong and the website wins. The site advertises 34.95 per month while checkout charges 37.95, which is 18 dollars extra on every semi annual order, and the same wrong figure sits in GoHighLevel so agents quote it too. The website price is correct. Correct the checkout, flag it to whoever is doing the GoHighLevel catalogue pass, and check whether any semi annual customer has already been overcharged.
  • Decision three, email stays optional at checkout. Sohib refused making email required, because most Liferun buyers are elderly and do not use email and a required field costs sales. Leave it optional and make sure phone alone is enough to identify and reach a buyer, since without email there is no receipt path.
  • Dependencies and constraints. Blocked on someone with Stripe Dashboard access reading the webhook event log, which is the one thing Hashir cannot do himself and the one thing that identifies the fault. Do not register a second webhook endpoint, one pointing at liferun.com already exists. Do not change plan structure or commercial terms, only the configured amounts and the add on mechanism. The GoHighLevel product catalogue audit is separate work and out of scope here.
  • done = a live test purchase creates the WordPress order and the GoHighLevel contact, Fall Detection is purchasable alongside a plan without a post checkout upsell, the semi annual checkout charges 34.95 per month matching the website, email is still optional, and the overcharge check result is posted here.

@Muhammad Hashir Faiz @Zayan Faiz

items.title: Agreement Cancellation
items.note: Drafted as a subitem under Document Handling 12471736810, which already owns the e signature and document workstream for this client, per the single item bias in drafting-rules.md.

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. On 3 September Tracy asked in the Maadi Law chat how to cancel an agreement that GoHighLevel had already sent out automatically, on a live matter for Rami Abushaqar. Sohib confirmed GoHighLevel has no direct cancel or void action on a sent document. Sharif escalated it as a real exposure in his own words: an unsigned agreement that stays open means a lead could sign it a year later, and the firm has no way to stop that.
  • Interim workaround already in use. Sohib found that Mark as declined closes the signature request, and Sharif told Tracy to use that wording until there is a proper mechanism. Treat that as the current standing instruction, not as the solution.
  • Deliverable one, establish what GoHighLevel actually supports. Confirm whether Mark as declined genuinely prevents the recipient from signing afterwards or only changes the internal status. Test it end to end on a dummy contact by marking a sent agreement declined and then opening the original signature link as the recipient. This is the load bearing question and everything else depends on the answer.
  • Deliverable two, add an expiry. If GoHighLevel supports a document or link expiry setting, turn it on with a sensible window so an unanswered agreement closes itself rather than staying open indefinitely. If it does not, say so on this item and propose the alternative, whether that is a scheduled automation that marks stale sent agreements declined or a change on the DocuSign path already being evaluated on this parent.
  • Deliverable three, write it down for Tracy. Document the confirmed cancel procedure in plain steps she can follow without asking, and post it here as well as sending it to her, since the answer currently exists only in a WhatsApp thread.
  • Dependencies and constraints. No client dependency, this can start immediately. Do not solve it by deleting the signature box or by editing the agreement text to say the proposal is void, which was Sohib's first suggestion before he found Mark as declined. Rami Abushaqar's open agreement is a live example, close it out as part of this work.
  • done = it is confirmed and documented whether a sent Maadi Law agreement can be genuinely cancelled so the recipient can no longer sign it, an expiry or equivalent automatic close is in place or ruled out with a named alternative, and Tracy has written steps she can follow.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. On 3 September Tracy reported that an old lead, Sandra Schneidwind, had automated texts sent to her about a week earlier, before the firm was using GoHighLevel for that lead at all. Every remaining historical record moved into GoHighLevel carries the same risk of messaging a client out of the blue, which for a law firm is a client facing exposure rather than an internal annoyance.
  • The mechanism, confirmed on 4 September. Sohib explained that Sandra was synced automatically out of Clio Grow without anyone realising it was happening. When Tracy entered her into Grow mid month she came across into GoHighLevel as a new contact, and creating that contact tripped the outbound automation. That accounts for the timing Tracy questioned, so the cause is no longer in doubt.
  • What is still unexplained. Tracy also saw nothing in her conversations view at the time the messages went out. The automatic Grow sync explains why the messages were sent but not why they were invisible to the person who owns intake. Sohib separately confirmed that a second contact Tracy could not find, Chiquita, does show up when searched by name, so this may be the same view or filter problem tracked on the Auto-Reject item rather than a second bug. Establish which it is and say so here.
  • Deliverable one, suppress automations on migrated and backfilled contacts. Contacts created by the Grow migration, by an automatic Clio sync, or by hand as historical backfill must not enter the new lead outbound sequences. Add a suppression condition, whether by tag, by source or by creation path, and state on this item which mechanism you used.
  • Deliverable two, check the blast radius. Sweep the migrated cohort for any other contact that received an outbound automated message it should not have, and list them here so Sharif and Tracy know the real number rather than assuming it was one record.
  • Deliverable three, close the automatic sync question. The Grow to GoHighLevel sync ran without the team knowing it was live. Confirm what else it is still bringing across and whether it should stay on at all while the migration is only at For Review.
  • Dependencies and constraints. Depends on the historical Grow migration subitem on this parent, which is at For Review with thirty held records and two identity collisions still undecided, so coordinate rather than sweeping those in blind. No client dependency. Do not switch off the new lead automations wholesale to solve this, genuine new leads must keep receiving them.
  • done = migrated, backfilled and Grow synced contacts are provably excluded from outbound automations with a test contact confirming it, the list of any other wrongly messaged contacts is posted here, and the conversations view question is either explained or handed to the Auto-Reject item.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context, a live defect on this path. On 3 September Tracy took a slip and fall intake for Chiquita Georges, rejected the case and believed she had moved it to the correct pipeline. After that the record vanished from her view entirely, no contact card and no matter, although Sharif could still find it in the conversations view.
  • Narrowed on 4 September. Sohib confirmed that Chiquita does show up in GoHighLevel if you search for her name. The record is therefore not lost, not merged away and not deleted. What is actually broken is narrower and more fixable: a rejected record drops out of the default view belonging to the person who owns intake, and is only reachable by knowing to search for it by name.
  • Why it still matters for this item. This item is building the branching behind the Not Qualified button. If a rejection only stays findable by name search, then in practice nobody can confirm the right email went out, reopen a case rejected in error, or review what was rejected last week without already knowing who to look for. That has to be settled before the one click action goes live, not after.
  • Deliverable one, fix the view rather than hunt the record. Establish which pipeline and stage a rejected case actually lands in, and why that stage falls outside Tracy’s default view while remaining visible to Sharif. If it is a permission or filter difference between their two views, correct Tracy’s view rather than asking her to search by name every time.
  • Deliverable two, give rejections a home. A rejected or disqualified record must be reachable through a named pipeline stage or a saved view that the intake user can open deliberately, not only through a search that assumes she already knows the name.
  • Deliverable three, cover the junk path too. This item already separates genuinely rejected cases from junk that gets disqualified silently. Confirm the fix holds for both branches, because the silent disqualify path is the more likely of the two to make a record disappear.
  • Dependencies and constraints. No client dependency, this can start immediately. Do not resolve it by turning off the disqualify behaviour, the silent junk path is deliberate and stays. Coordinate with the Clio Migration work, since a rejected case also has to reflect correctly back through the Clio Manage sync, and the migrated contact item on that parent is chasing a related view question.
  • done = Tracy can open a saved view or pipeline stage and see both a rejected case and a silently disqualified case without searching by name, confirmed with one test record of each.
